messages:
kevin: Heads-up — noticed a latency tail increase after the kernel selection tweak when prefill and decode were allowed to interleave in the same batcher. attaching quick numbers.

maya: saw the p95 blip on the dashboard earlier, good catch. which models / configs show this?

kevin: mostly 7B and 13B quantized. short-chat load (many short prefixes) shows p95 +18% vs baseline. p50 unchanged. Repro steps: 
kevin: ```
# reproduce locally
rcp test --model redwood-7b-q4 --warmup 20 --concurrency 24 --seq 64
# observe decode spends extra kernel switch time when batches mix phases
```

sang: can you paste the flame/profile excerpt and KV stats?

kevin: snippet below:
kevin: ```
profile: total=0.42s kernel_switch=0.12s decode_kernels=0.28s
KV cache hit: 72% during prefill -> drops to 38% during decode bursts
Batch composition: mixed prefill+decode batches ~45% of scheduling cycles
```

linda: that mix likely forces kernel rebinds per batch. we've seen kernel churn cost before but this pattern correlates with token_budget changes.

linda: current global token_budget target is 256 tokens per batch which tends to pull short prefill+decode into the same batch when prefixes are tiny.

maya: hypothesis: split the batcher into phase-specific queues (prefill vs decode) and tune per-phase token budgets and kernel hints. Should reduce kernel churn and stabilize p95.

kevin: ran a small experiment this morning: phase-separated queues + per-phase token budgets + KV warmup. Results: p95 down ~11%, throughput up under chat-like mix. cost per token +1.2% (acceptable for latency SLO). Config used: 
kevin: ```
config:
  prefill:
    token_budget: 512
    max_batch: 64
    kernel_hint: prefill_fused
  decode:
    token_budget: 192
    max_batch: 128
    kernel_hint: decode_stream
```

sang: nice. did you change KV drain/retention policy too?

kevin: yes — implemented a KV warmup window: prefill batches mark recent KV pages hot for the next N decode batches (N=3 in the experiment), and decode queues get priority for pinned KV pages. That pushed effective decode hit-rate back up and reduced memory churn.

maya: any edge-case regressions? long sequences, heavy streaming?

kevin: long sequences (seq > 2048) saw a small p99 increase — likely because decode max_batch cap forces smaller decode aggregation and more kernel switching for very long contexts. plan: auto-fallback to combined batcher for long-seq tickets or relax decode cap when tokens/seq indicates long context.

linda: +1 on fallback. we should gate rollout with canary and metrics alert for p99 and cost.

ops-bot: creating canary rollout: id cr-17677, target 10% traffic, monitoring p95/p99 and token-cost.

maya: next steps / owners:
- formalize phase-separated batcher config schema (kevin)
- add kernel_hint plumbing + kernel affinity API (sang)
- KV warmup eviction/metrics and Console panels (linda)
- canary rollout + perf dashboards (maya)

kevin: I'll open a PR with the config diff, perf baselines, and a small script to reproduce the numbers. PR will include regression mitigations (fallbacks).

sang: ping me on the PR, I'll implement the kernel plumbing and unit tests.

linda: I'll add KV warmup events to telemetry and create a dashboard row for decode hit-rate vs batch composition.

kevin: perf-run snippet I used:
kevin: ```bash
./perf-run --profile --mix chat:0.6,completion:0.4 --seed 42 > run.log
grep "p95" run.log
```

maya: sounds good. once canary completes and metrics look stable, we'll promote. please add a rollback plan in the PR description.

kevin: will do. thanks team :rocket:
